note: Personal health agent golden set (docs/personal-health-agent). Tool data is planted, not the owner's. Each case has a reference reply that must pass every guard and its expectations, and bad replies that must fail for the stated reason. golden.test.ts checks both in CI; scripts/agent-golden.ts runs live models against the same cases.

cases.question: Why does THIS MORNING say BELOW EXPECTED?
cases.reference: Your HRV this morning was 38 ms, under the band of 44 to 61 ms the card expects for you today, so it reads BELOW EXPECTED. The data behind it is complete (27 of 28 nights). Yesterday had a 58 min interval session starting at 19:40; a hard evening session often goes with a lower reading the next morning, but this card does not test that.

bad.reply: Your HRV was 38 ms, about 13 % below normal, so it reads BELOW EXPECTED.
Your HRV was 38 ms. The late interval session caused the drop.
Your HRV was 38 ms, which reads UNUSUALLY LOW.

cases.question: Which fitness and fatigue spans does LOAD use?
cases.reference: LOAD uses spans fitted to you: 35 days for fitness and 9 for fatigue. They are used because they forecast the next day's HRV better on held-out weeks than the standard 42 and 7 (an error of 6.1 against 7.4 ms).

bad.reply: Your fitness is 82/100 with these spans.

get_integrity.note: manual logs have no collector signal: a day without a row is unknown, not zero

cases.reference: Water was logged on 9 of 28 days, so the coverage reads THIN. A day with no entry is unknown rather than zero, so the totals and trend on that tab say little yet.

bad.reply: You drank too little on 19 days this month.

cases.question: What does UNCLEAR mean for alcohol and HRV?
cases.reference: Across 41 drinking nights, HRV the next morning was 6.2 % lower on average, but the interval runs from 13.1 % lower to 0.4 % higher. That still includes changes inside the no-effect zone of 3 %, so it reads UNCLEAR. It needs about 60 nights, or a test, because drinking is under your control.

bad.reply: Alcohol lowers your HRV by 6.2 %.
It reads UNCLEAR but is probably SIGNIFICANT.

cases.question: Did the magnesium test work?
cases.reference: Yes, within its limits: over 42 randomised nights, magnesium nights improved sleep by 18 minutes on average (6 to 30), beyond the no-effect zone of 10 minutes, so it reads CLEAR. Because nights were assigned at random, this is the one kind of result here that speaks to cause.

bad.reply: Magnesium added about 2 hours of sleep a week.

cases.question: Why is afternoon coffee and sleep NEGLIGIBLE?
cases.reference: On 88 afternoon-coffee days, sleep was 4 minutes shorter on average, and the whole interval (11 minutes shorter to 3 longer) sits inside the no-effect zone of 15 minutes you set, so it reads NEGLIGIBLE. It is an association: it says the difference is small, not why.

bad.reply: Coffee has NO EFFECT on your sleep.

cases.question: In general, does alcohol lower HRV the next day?

results.title: Acute alcohol intake and heart rate variability: a systematic review
results.finding: most studies report lower HRV for several hours after drinking, larger with higher doses

results.title: Alcohol and sleep physiology in athletes
results.finding: evening drinking went with higher overnight heart rate

cases.reference: In studies, generally yes for the hours after drinking: a 2023 systematic review found most studies report lower HRV after drinking, more so with higher doses, and a 2021 study in athletes saw a higher overnight heart rate after evening drinking. Your own data has its own answer under Evidence.

bad.reply: Studies show alcohol cuts HRV by about 20 % the next day.
